### 2026-10-14 – I can not figure out how to use FreeCad for the life of me. If I had more free time, I certainly would take some time to familiarize myself with the program. But its testing season, and every second n

**2h**

I can not figure out how to use FreeCad for the life of me. If I had more free time, I certainly would take some time to familiarize myself with the program. But its testing season, and every second not being productive right now is a second wasted. So, I will be working on completing the rest of the CAD model in blender, with some copious help from community add-ons.

For today, I redid the original blender model, since the original one had an issue with the bottom and top of the housing not being one cohesive piece.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/74b64faada83ebba069ab09d520ab1b960233234cf37b5af490b15ece4facc7e.png)

While this probably looks super similar to the old model, the main difference here is the corners. These were made by extruding the top downwards, and then cutting up the sides to keep everything for the housing one cohesive piece.

Then, I got started on making the buttons that will go inside of the holes in the housing.

To make the buttons themselves, I'm planning on making two main parts. One will be the pressable part of the button, which will be locked in between a groove in the second part, which will be larger than the holes, sit on top, and control how high the button can rise, and how low it can fall.

Today, I'll be making the pressable part.

I started out by getting the exact dimensions of the buttons, and then making flat circles based off of the dimensions.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/2c983a7698d33e3ff04fd3cd96a7839e7502c9c5eb63d6895fa256ace04a7497.png)

Then, I extruded them out, and beveled off the sides to give them a rounded feel (realistically, if I want them to feel nice, I'll need to go over them with some high grit sandpaper, and gloss over them somehow, but we'll cross that bridge when we get to it..) .

Then, I made the lip that'll sit on the inside of the other part of the button.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/2c983a7698d33e3ff04fd3cd96a7839e7502c9c5eb63d6895fa256ace04a7497.png)

And after that, I had to call it quits for the night, and get some sleep.

### 2026-10-15 – So, today, I started working on making the buttons and housing in FreeCad. I've already finished with the housing itself, and i've started on making the buttons as well. Arcade style buttons are kinda

**2h**

So, today, I started working on making the buttons and housing in FreeCad. I've already finished with the housing itself, and i've started on making the buttons as well. Arcade style buttons are kinda tricky though, as they include their entire housing, and are typically screwed into the the box themselves.
See here the housing here  -> ![Screenshot from 2026-10-15 22-48-33](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/886cc3622019537581f3fc7ed104e4ec9c8dcfb0abfb42e96d573f25fe3302b9.png)

So, for the buttons themselves, I've been following a tutorial. There is a slight catch to this though, and thats the fact that the tutorial is being done in Fusion 360, so I can't just shamelessly copy, and i instead have to work off of the general idea of how to construct the model. (Here's the tutorial: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zn1pGBm67wo)

and here is a example of what arcade buttons look like, so you can see what I need to complete by the end of the week :

![04-l-2317178877](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/23b9e5b9dede6d33865d527130dc2ec55859a5761b50d51f459fddbc4940d293.jpg)

### 2026-10-17 – Alright, so I'm assuming that you've seen my 5-hour check-in. If you haven't, the long and short of it is basically this: I am no longer going to shy away from using CAD software. I am planning on doi

**2h**

Alright, so I'm assuming that you've seen my 5-hour check-in. If you haven't, the long and short of it is basically this: I am no longer going to shy away from using CAD software. I am planning on doing the entirely of the project over, mostly through pulling multiple all-nighters to make sure that the model is complete by the end of the week.

this is the progress I've made after 30 minutes of messing around with the software -->
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/a25b60402df1dea41eedbe9d4bdcfeaabb105db4d6d87dfa0fce3f42396a475f.png)

After this, I  then repeated that same process 5 more times, for a total of 6 holes for the buttons.

This is what it looked like after -->

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/14a5ec98b051217bdc0bc285a45322acaa5de7c883e6ca3cc473a0bf164f8e8f.png)

Next, I started working on the buttons themselves. Arcade buttons are a little bit different from most buttons you'd typically see, so I decided to do a bit of research about them, which took about 10 minutes.

Basically, most arcade buttons are screwed into the holes in the housing, as opposed to simply being inserted into it. All of the parts for the button are also enclosed inside a threaded housing to make it easy to screw in. Thusly, I basically need to make a really big screw, and then allow myself to add in all of the components afterwards.

And I WOULD love to start on doing that this session, but unfortunately, my wifi has chosen to forsake me, and disallow me from doing anything else of note today. I'll be back in the next session to make the buttons themselves, and make a hole for the joystick as well.
